dlg.maeca.cb_knelt.0.intent: she saw you kneel to Greymuzzle
dlg.maeca.cb_knelt.0.note: Narrator for the look at your knees. 'He let you.' amazed. The last sentence hurt, plain.

dlg.maeca.blood.0.note: Narrator: she stops and sniffs. Curt orders. 'It took it off me.' quiet, a confession.

dlg.maeca.blind_leave.0.note: Care disguised as a road report.

dlg.maeca.watch_morning.0.note: Narrator for the stretch. 'Most can't.' a small compliment.

dlg.maeca.told_true.0.note: Narrator: she almost smiles. The poaching joke fond.

dlg.maeca.told_true.1.note: Thinking. 'Read me something, one day.' shy, then 'Not now.' quick.

dlg.maeca.told_true.2.note: Plain respect, with Ashford under it.

dlg.maeca.told_true.3.note: Narrator: a long breath. The cave mouth line very quiet. 'We'd have got on.' tender.

dlg.maeca.told_little.0.note: Narrator around her. 'I keep mine.' kind.

dlg.maeca.blind3_morning.0.note: Narrator: grey light, her head on your chest. Close and still: the hare and the bear. 'I counted between.' A pause where the name would be. Narrator: she goes out. 'Go on. Holloway'll count us.' steadier.

dlg.maeca.blind3_m_no.0.note: 'No.' Narrator: not unkind. Her old rule, softened.

dlg.maeca.say_sella.0.note: Narrator: the cup. Level. 'I mind not knowing.' honest and quiet.

dlg.maeca.say_sella_you.0.note: Narrator for the long look. 'We'll see.' guarded.

dlg.maeca.blind.2.note: Low and close, unhurried; the boots one action at a time.

dlg.maeca.blind_walk.0.note: Narrator plain and starlit; a beat before 'and is answered'. Maeca just above a breath, naming neighbours by their voices. Narrator plain: the narrator never shows a feeling.
dlg.maeca.blind_walk.0.beats: ...a wolf calls [beat] and is answered. | Him. [beat] And the bitch with the white foot. | She walks on.

dlg.maeca.blind_walk.1.note: Narrator plain: the narrator never shows a feeling. The gift is the fact itself; don't lean on it.
dlg.maeca.blind_walk.1.beats: The Old Road, the wreck, the frost. [beat] You know the way now, and she lets you walk in front, [beat] which she has never done.

dlg.maeca.blind_fire.0.note: One action at a time; the look across the fire held.

dlg.maeca.blind_dark.0.note: The inversion (your skin colder than her feet) is nearly funny: straight and level, don't darken it. The last sentence hangs, not drops: the player's choice follows.
dlg.maeca.blind_dark.0.beats: Afterwards, in the dark under the hides, she puts her feet against your legs, [beat] and flinches: [beat] you're colder than they are. She starts to take them back—

dlg.maeca.blind_dark.1.intent: the Pack lies down round you; she asks what you were
dlg.maeca.blind_dark.1.hides: she is counting your heart between her sentences; it is slow, and at night it can stop for a count of seven
dlg.maeca.blind_dark.1.note: Narrator plain, the Pack's arrival a held breath. Maeca flat on 'They don't do that', because she can't afford the wonder. 'What were you?' careful, not curious: no stress on 'were', even weight, asked to the dark, after a real count of about three seconds.
dlg.maeca.blind_dark.1.beats: ...listening the way she listens to the Hollow. [breath] Outside, in the frost, you hear them come: soft feet, a long way round, [beat] and then a sigh, [beat] and then another. ... [beat] She lifts her head. | They don't do that. [beat] Not for me. Not for anyone. | She lies back down, her ear where it was. | You walk quiet. You came into my Hollow and knelt to him, and he let you. [beat] You never talk about before. | Against your chest you feel her lips move, without a sound. | [silence 3 s] What were you?

dlg.maeca.blind_dark.2.hides: she is counting your heart between her sentences
dlg.maeca.blind_dark.2.note: As blind_dark.1 without the Pack. 'What were you?' careful, no stress on 'were', after a real count of about three seconds.
dlg.maeca.blind_dark.2.beats: ...listening the way she listens to the Hollow. | You walk quiet. You never talk about before. | Against your chest you feel her lips move, without a sound. | [silence 3 s] What were you?

dlg.maeca.blind2_feet.0.note: The scars described plainly; her words are hers.

dlg.rav.leg_held.0.note: Narrator: the cup set down. '...Did he.' A long time. Professional pride as armour: 'I'm a good doctor.' cracking. Kind dismissal.

dlg.rav.back_room.0.note: Plain; the moving jar and the trophy needle as plain facts.

dlg.rav.back_room_look.0.note: Alarmed 'You came.' Doctor's orders, joking. Narrator through the exam. 'Cold as a cellar step.' quiet and worried. The last lines a joke covering real alarm.

dlg.rav.back_room_drink.0.note: Dry about the cups. The last sentence a soft confession.

dlg.rav.back_room_kiss.0.note: Narrator through the kiss and the hand. 'Not yet, pal.' gentle. His reasons plain. 'I'm always here.' rueful; the worrying part dry.

dlg.rav.came_back.0.note: Narrator: sober, shaved. 'You came back.' Long look. Dry about Rook's. Then plain: no talk of it. 'I'm a doctor today.' steadying himself.

dlg.rav.came_back_sorry.0.note: Firm and kind. 'I'll not be able to hear it twice.' near breaking.

dlg.vonnra.fortune.1.note: As fortune.0. 'No charge, this once.' is the call's twin (C01): the same phrasing, close and quiet across a table, so a listener can find it.

dlg.keegan.supper.0.intent: invites you to supper, by the book
dlg.keegan.supper.0.note: 'I am on watch.' prim. Narrator: the bread. The citation proud; 'It does not say whose morale.' a slip of mischief. The stone warning earnest.

dlg.keegan.supper_wends.0.note: Lecturer's pride; the chiasmus recited. 'It has kept neither.' quiet. Narrator: she smiles at the road. Flustered about the joke; 'It's late.' a contraction slipping.

dlg.keegan.supper_age.0.note: Narrator: sidelong. A joke at herself; the last line a smile.

dlg.keegan.supper_letters.0.note: Narrator holds the silence. Very precise, very hurt. 'That was an example of correctio.' brittle. Thanks sincere. 'I am also not a fool.' quiet and firm.

dlg.keegan.supper_read.0.note: Narrator: delighted. The handbook quoted with relish; 'In protest.' Narrator for the reading. The last line amazed and shy.

dlg.keegan.supper_ch4.0.note: Narrator: the book closed. 'No.' gently. Narrator holds the quiet.

dlg.keegan.supper_hand.0.note: Narrator for the hands. 'I am on duty.' unsteady. The rhetoric lesson a shield. 'Goodnight.' soft.

dlg.keegan.supper_end.0.note: 'Goodnight.' Narrator: as you go. 'Mine. I checked.' delighted.

dlg.sella.free_night.2.note: Low and close, slower; the look given room.

quote.note: A professional's line that happens to be true.
A warning dressed as a joke.
She has noticed the cold, and the joke is how she makes it nothing.
Into your ear, delighted to make you jump.

dlg.sella.stairs_room.4.note: The two mothers a nice turn, unhurried.

quote.note: A professional's line that happens to be true.
A warning dressed as a joke.
She has noticed the cold, and the joke is how she makes it nothing.
Into your ear, delighted to make you jump.

dlg.sella.stairs_rules.0.note: Narrator through the cold, long and quiet. Then her rules, steadying herself with the patter.

dlg.sella.stop_paid.0.note: Narrator: no sulk. Practical with the coins. 'Either's all right, love.' meant.

dlg.sella.rest_bed.0.note: Rapid little orders; the chair line dry.

dlg.sella.rest_dark.0.note: Low and close; the watching very quiet.

dlg.sella.rest_morning.0.note: Narrator: her hand on your chest. Quiet wonder at the cold. Then warm and wry: 'Best money I ever made.' doubles (she'll be paid for it twice): play it as a joke and nothing more; the listener finds the rest.
dlg.sella.rest_morning.0.hides: she knows who pays for a thing like this, and unless she has stopped selling you, Vonnra will have it by noon

dlg.sella.rest_morning.1.note: Narrator: she doesn't count it. 'Rich and bored.' a grin.

dlg.sella.door.0.note: Narrator: her boots. Plain about danger; 'I'll not say which.' closed.

dlg.sella.door_south.0.note: Narrator: she checks her hair, not looking at you. 'And somebody who knocks.' quiet.

dlg.sella.free_decline.0.note: 'Your loss, love. Literally; I'm worth a fortune.' a real joke, with a laugh. '...No, it's all right.' a beat, 'It is.': convincing herself. 'I don't ask twice.' is pride. Narrator: the pat. Brisk kindness.
dlg.sella.free_decline.0.beats: Your loss, love. Literally; I'm worth a fortune. [laugh] | ...No, it's all right. [beat] It is. I'll not ask twice. I don't ask twice. | Go on. Rook's stew's still warm.

dlg.sella.free_ask.0.note: Narrator for the look. Wry logic. 'Come on.' twice, the second a little shaky.

dlg.sella.free_stairs.0.note: The creak 'loud as a shout' given its beat; then quieter.

dlg.sella.free_door.0.beats: I keep thinking about you sitting on my bed telling me where you're from. Knowing who'd hear it by morning. | Nobody does that. [beat] Nobody's ever done that.

dlg.sella.free_door.1.note: A small laugh at her own lie.

dlg.sella.free_want.0.note: Narrator: the breath. Not tears: she is never pitiful. Telling you she might cry is the most naked thing she says, and she says it dry; then she decides. 'Yes.' twice, the second firmer. 'Come here.' soft.

dlg.sella.free_stop.0.note: Narrator: the held breath. The Rook joke soft.

quote.note: Her forehead against the door and her back to you. She has never shot it; the word is the decision.

dlg.sella.free_m_downstairs.0.note: Narrator: she laughs. The turn 'No. You wouldn't.' honest.

dlg.sella.free_m_who.0.note: Narrator: the quilt. Her honesty stumbling; a beat where the name would be.

quote.note: Smiling as she pushes you off: the truth under the joke.

dlg.sella.refuse_roost.0.note: Narrator at the door and the coins. Cool, not cruel. 'Come back when I can't.' quiet.

dlg.greymuzzle.show.1.note: As show.0; the lip lifting given its beat.

dlg.cin_drowned_fire.prints.0.intent: your own prints come from the river
dlg.cin_drowned_fire.prints.0.note: Two plain facts; a pause, then 'None go down to it.' on its own.
dlg.cin_drowned_fire.prints.0.beats: Prints in the frost, your own. They come up from the river. [beat] None go down to it.
dlg.cin_drowned_fire.prints.0.time_note: about 0.7 s of pause before 'None go down to it.'

dlg.cin_first_light.face.0.note: Plain and slow; the strangeness is in the words.
dlg.cin_first_light.face.0.time_note: the cut then holds three seconds of silence

dlg.cin_none_cross.call.0.intent: the Order's evening call, heard through water
dlg.cin_none_cross.call.0.note: Sung low, as a dirge: two phrases of about three seconds with a short breath between; the second trails off as he rises.
dlg.cin_none_cross.call.0.time_note: two phrases of about 3.0 s with 0.8 s between, the second trailing off

dlg.cin_none_cross.lie_down.0.intent: the Order's word for the dead, said over a grave
dlg.cin_none_cross.lie_down.0.note: Not a threat: said to her as you would say it over a grave.

dlg.cin_none_cross.none.0.intent: the ford's rule, not a threat
dlg.cin_none_cross.none.0.note: Every word set down like a stone; no louder than 'Lie down.' The capitals are the subtitle's, not the performance's.

dlg.cin_heart_goes_down.morning.0.intent: the man under the Warden asks the lamp
dlg.cin_heart_goes_down.morning.0.note: Not the giant's voice: a plain, tired man of sixty, the accent worn off, no boom. Quiet enough that the subtitle is the only certain thing.

dlg.cin_heart_goes_down.nobodys.0.intent: Grimtunnel finds the heart still lit
dlg.cin_heart_goes_down.nobodys.0.note: Delight, a child's at a pie.

dlg.cin_heart_goes_down.downstairs.0.note: A sniff before it; the glee gone, curious. Then the laugh in the breath after.
dlg.cin_heart_goes_down.downstairs.0.time_note: the words 1.6 to 2.0 s, after the sniff

dlg.cin_heart_goes_down.grateful.0.note: Half over his shoulder as he dives. 'surface-m—' breaks off: he cannot finish 'meat' at her. A sniff, then the rest to himself.

dlg.cin_iron_marker.verse1.0.note: Sung simply and not well; he can't sing and nobody minds.

dlg.cin_raid_on_the_roost.bairns.0.note: 'Ha! HA.' then cold: the bairns. 'Mind where you swing.' a grim joke.

dlg.cin_raid_on_the_roost.last.0.note: Breath failing. Narrator: a laugh. 'Now we've both said it.'

dlg.cin_dig_boils_over.pump.0.note: 'PUMP' stressed. Then oily calm: 'Downstairs is PATIENT.'

dlg.cin_behind_the_door.nondum.0.note: Latin: NON-dum. The narrator does not translate aloud; the subtitle does.

dlg.cin_road_back.wat.0.note: Quiet and low, the voice nearly going; no whisper (a whispered bass loses him).

say.dabd6c78b40d.intent: reads a dead man and his last words
say.dabd6c78b40d.note: The book's three lines read as written words, plainly, one after another.

say.178e6dd0ad78.intent: a dead man speaks to you alone
say.178e6dd0ad78.note: A hush: one of his four whispers.

say.20b15596c09c.say: A door of black stone, smooth as glass. Cut over it, words in a dead tongue: hic legio septima sepelivit quod urere non potuit. Under them, a violet sigil you cannot read. It hums against your teeth.
say.20b15596c09c.note: The Latin said slowly, as old words.

say.8591ecfe4019.note: A hush: one of his four whispers.

say.1a1877c48374.say: Jory. Jory Coyle. Is my uncle... Is he...

dlg.cin_drowned_fire.lamp.0.intent: a lamp, and a voice up the road
dlg.cin_drowned_fire.lamp.0.note: Plain and quiet; no pause needed.

say.e6fc0151e69a.intent: a lamp, and a voice up the road
say.e6fc0151e69a.note: Plain and quiet; no pause needed.

dlg.cin_drowned_fire.call.0.intent: a toll-keeper waving a traveller through
dlg.cin_drowned_fire.call.0.wants: the risen traveller up the road and into her town before dawn
dlg.cin_drowned_fire.call.0.note: Far off and thinned by the cold, never raised; the frost carries it, close as if at the shoulder. The pause before 'No charge' is her deciding to. The game adds the distance (the 'far' effect): record it dry and close.
dlg.cin_drowned_fire.call.0.beats: Come up, traveller. [beat] ...No charge, this once.

say.bc92c07d79db.wants: the risen traveller up the road and into her town before dawn
